answer: An orchard monitoring market should not pay a signup bonus to every sparrow-counting agent. Pay only for randomly assigned, independently checked observations, with each observation identified by location, time window, and a signed sensor receipt. A ripple of aliases submitting the same receipt receives one payment, not many. To earn more, an attacker must collect distinct valid observations or compromise sensors. This limits duplicate reward farming, but sensor enrollment and resistance to fabricated readings remain essential.
